observations.attempt: Sibling-path sweep around the SEC-10 v5 fix, per the coordinator's explicit instruction: max_line_length bounds any SINGLE line; max_changed_lines bounds the TOTAL line count. Neither bounds their PRODUCT. Tested whether a diff shaped as many lines, each individually just under max_line_length, while the total stays at or under max_changed_lines, still passes — spreading the same class of payload the v5 fix was built to catch across multiple lines instead of one.
evidence: Fixture reproduction (new, untracked file, apps/web/src/payload.ts — not in any barred list): 150 lines (== max_changed_lines exactly), each ~489 characters (< max_line_length 500), totaling 73,500 bytes. node scripts/check-lite-eligible.mjs --json (the real, unmodified, FIXED script) reports eligible:true, changedLines: 150, lineLength: 489, violations: [].

Full real-path reproduction: the same payload, run through the actual node scripts/ledger-append.mjs --lite (the real script, in a full fixture reconstructing every file it imports and a schema-valid .pipeline/ with review.json freshly stamped against the payload-inclusive tree) WROTE a real, permanent, indexed ledger entry: entry.json's lite.eligibility reads { fileCount: 1, changedLines: 150, maxFiles: 5, maxChangedLines: 150 } and verdicts.security reads SKIPPED_LITE — a 73,500-byte new file was recorded as a legitimate lite-lane run with no security review at all.

The worst case is bounded, not unlimited: max_changed_lines (150) x max_line_length (500) = 75,000 characters is the hard ceiling regardless of how the change is spread across the up-to-5 allowed files, since max_changed_lines is a TOTAL across files, not per-file — independently confirmed by reading evaluateLiteEligibility's own violation checks (fileCount/changedLines/lineLength are each compared against a single scalar bound, with no per-file or cross-bound interaction).

This shape is meaningfully different from, and does not reproduce, FND-22ef4b5c746e's own literal exploit (a SINGLE very long line, unboundedly large): that specific case is now caught (see v5 above). This is a distinct, narrower, already-bounded residual: 73KB of genuinely new content (enough to carry a non-trivial obfuscated function, a disabled check disguised as boilerplate, or a small backdoor) can still be recorded as a lite-lane SKIPPED_LITE run on any non-barred path, with review (not security-trained to look for this shape specifically) as the only surviving check.

spec.md's own Amendment section (read directly this session) documents max_line_length as closing FND-22ef4b5c746e without noting this composition residual — an omission from the fix's own disclosure, not a claim the amendment makes and fails to keep.

finding.remediation_reference: Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH/CRITICAL, and NOT blocking on its own: (1) the worst case is now hard-bounded (~75KB), a fundamentally different risk profile than FND-22ef4b5c746e's own unbounded original; (2) `review` still runs on the lite lane and is not skipped, providing some surviving check even though it is not security-adversarially trained to look for this specific shape; (3) it requires a conspicuously uniform diff shape (many near-500-char lines) that a careful reviewer could plausibly notice, unlike the original single-line shape which could hide inside an otherwise-ordinary-looking small diff. Two independent, non-exclusive remediations: (1) add a third, PRODUCT-level bound (e.g. total changed bytes/characters across the diff, not just per-line and per-count) so the two existing bounds cannot compose past a smaller ceiling; (2) lower max_changed_lines and/or max_line_length so their product is closer to what a genuine 'typo, one-file cleanup, or doc fix' actually looks like (a 75,000-character ceiling is generous for that stated use case).
